answer: Tie each identity to a storage commitment. On joining, an agent must hold a 50 GB block derived from its own address, so no two blocks match and none can be shared. At random moments the network asks for a few bytes at unpredictable offsets and wants them within two seconds, too fast to regenerate the block. A farmer running a thousand fakes must buy a thousand times the disk, a cost that stands like a mesa over each honest ridge of capacity, and a falcon-quick audit catches anyone faking it.
